I went online September Thursday 03,2026 at 18:28 pm.I booked a vacation package all inclusive resort. I accidentally did a typo error on my name. I only noticed it at 19:30pm . I promptly called the 1877-735-5633 number to have it corrected. The First Lady to answer the phone told me this can’t be corrected. I was shocked beyond words. I immediately started trouble shooting with different ideas.
1. Do I have to buy another ticket??
2. Do I have to buy two new packages
Then cancel the other
3. Do I have just go to the airport and walk up to the Air Transit Counter and have it corrected there?
4. She then transferred the call to another travel agent
Who said she would be able to do the correction for a fee. She then told me she had to call Air Transit and put me on hold for 2 1/2 hours. She then offered me the call back option. So at 21:00 pm , she called me back. Only to say she was unable to help me. But I should try calling tomorrow.
September Friday 4,2026 decided to call air transit myself. To see if I can have this issue corrected in a timely fashion. I was on hold for two hours and 18 minutes when I finally got to speak to a travel agent.He was very polite, but said I had to be transferred to the package department. A young lady came on the phone only to advise me. She was unable to do the corrections for me and I would have to try to contact Sell off vacation .com myself. They will be able to make all the Necessary correction in a timely fashion. I’m just a little confused as to why this is taking so long and very disappointed. It has been less than 24 hours since I’ve made my booking and I’m still unable to make the correction. Disappointed traveller

what i have to say is from personal experience over multiple years of reaching out and receiving help from family's first.

family's first is always willing to help, they have/had a lot of support, but only if they deem you worthy.

as their name states, they help families, but they also have been asked to help the less fortunate, homeless, or drug addicted in fort Saskatchewan.

the homeless and drug addicted are mocked and made fun of, they are judged and thought of as a threat once they leave.

not once over the years have i had an incident with any homeless or drug addicted, in fact one/two have actually helped me with an issue.

they are not wanted, they are pushed even farther away from help.

there are some workers there that wholeheartedly believe that they need to help, not just who they think they should but to help the ones who have no one else. those people are hero's and in my eyes make family first what it was, help for everyone.

i am disappointed in the current management and direction family's first has gone, seeing as its the only place available in the fort it will be a difficult decision but i will not be retuning.

if you struggle with mental health, are homeless or drug addicted, it is never too late. whenever you are ready, support is there to help you, but please do your research and find a better alternative other than family's first.

one_star_reviews.text:
We completed two kitchen projects with this company. The installation was handled through the Saskatoon office, while most communication was through the Calgary office so we will be leaving this review in both places appropriately.

Both kitchens were incorrectly templated and measured. They also failed to show up with even the proper materials on installation day to complete. The resulting countertops were unusable for our project and quite literally could not have even be installed that day due to not fitting or covering required gaps in cabinets and an entire sit up overhang was completely missed. As I write this review, the countertops from both kitchens are fully wasted material and are still sitting on the floor months later because they could not be used. We ultimately had to hire another contractor to redo the entire project(s).

Throughout the process, the company blamed us for issues that that arose from their templating and measurement errors such as referencing our rough numbers used to get preliminary quotes (as they are not local and require this to even get started). Even when mistakes were identified, we were unable to obtain an acceptable resolution.

Our concerns were dismissed, conversations were often confrontational, and the company refused to take responsibility for the problems and blamed us for countertops being the wrong size even though their own contract verbiage and common industry practice of required templating disproves this. The only solution offered was for us to pay additional money to have their own mistakes corrected.

As a result, we have incurred thousands of dollars in additional costs and are currently pursuing litigation to recover our losses.

Based on our experience with two separate kitchens, I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
*Extremely disappointing experience, and a serious lack of transparency*

I had a very disappointing experience shopping at this Harry Rosen location.

I purchased a Creed fragrance, only to realize after returning home that I had paid significantly more than I would have, buying the exact same product directly from Creed’s own website, roughly 35% more.

I had not even opened the packaging, so I returned to the store right away hoping to exchange it for something more reasonably priced. Only then was I informed that all fragrances are final sale.

My biggest issue is not simply the final-sale policy. It is that the salesperson who processed my purchase never disclosed this policy before taking my payment. For a high-priced item that cannot be returned or exchanged, this is important information that should be clearly communicated to the customer at the time of purchase.

What made the experience considerably worse was how the situation was handled afterward. Rather than acknowledging that the final-sale condition had not been communicated to me, the staff simply hid behind the policy and made no meaningful effort to resolve the situation. Most insulting of all, while explaining why they would not accept the unopened product, the salesperson even implied that I could have replaced the contents of the bottle.

Being treated with suspicion after spending a substantial amount of money at a store that positions itself around premium products and customer service was incredibly disrespectful.

A final-sale policy is one thing. Failing to disclose it before the sale, then effectively questioning the customer’s honesty when they raise the issue, is another.

This experience completely changed my perception of Harry Rosen and will unfortunately be the last time I shop at this location.

After an initial hand surgery performed by Dr. Lessard, I discovered he also had a cosmetic surgery practice. I therefore chose to have him perform my procedure.

My decision wasn't motivated by any particular problem: I was simply tired of having large breasts and initially wanted to have my implants removed. The surgery, performed in March 2024 at a cost of $14,000, also included a breast lift and liposuction under my arms.
I noticed the problems after the surgery, and they persist to this day, a little over two years later: complete loss of sensation, deformation of the left nipple, an artificial appearance of the right nipple, significant scarring, and excess skin under my arms. I met with Dr. Lessard a few times after the surgery to discuss the condition of my nipples and scars. During one of these meetings, he asked me what my problem was, in a tone I perceived as condescending. He also told me he found the procedure difficult to perform. In light of my experience and the results obtained, I believe he lacked the necessary skills to perform this type of procedure.

I have initiated legal proceedings to assert my rights. The significant and lasting consequences I am suffering cannot be trivialized or ignored. No patient should have to accept such harm. A doctor cannot make such mistakes, leave a patient with such a detrimental outcome, and shirk his responsibilities. I will therefore continue my legal action.
This deserves zero stars....

one_star_reviews.text:
Very (very) poor after-sales service.

I had my garage roof redone by BGA Construction about four years ago. Unfortunately, the work doesn't seem to have been done correctly, as there's been a water leak in one spot since it was installed.

Since then, I've made numerous follow-up calls to get the situation rectified. I even went to their offices twice to follow up. Each time, I was assured that someone would come to assess the problem and make the necessary repairs. To this day, no one has shown up.

Unfortunately, this isn't the first time we've had this kind of experience with this company. We also hired them around the same time for work at my office, and it took almost two years before they finally came to install a door threshold that had been overlooked during the initial work.

I can understand that a problem or an oversight can happen. What I find much harder to accept is having to make countless calls, follow-ups, and even site visits for years without the promised repairs being carried out.

After four years of dealing with a water leak following roofing work, I absolutely do not recommend this company. In my opinion, their after-sales service is inadequate (nonexistent!) and the promised follow-ups are simply not done.

Nobody goes to a food bank by choice. With Toronto rents reaching extremely high levels, especially under the current Doug Ford government, many people are being pushed into situations where they have no choice but to rely on food banks just to get by.

People who use food banks are already vulnerable and struggling. They deserve dignity, patience, and respect. Unfortunately, my experience at this food bank has been very disappointing.

Some of the staff have been disrespectful and arrogant toward people who are simply there because they need help. The other day, an Asian female staff member literally yelled at me because I picked up milk and cereal together and told me I could only take one. I asked, “How am I supposed to eat cereal without milk?” There was absolutely no reason to speak to me that way.

The quantity of food has also gone down significantly over the past four weeks. Today, we received only one milk, six tiny eggs, three onions, and three green peppers. How are people supposed to survive on that?

I understand that donations and food supplies can fluctuate, and I appreciate that food banks provide an important service. But when people are struggling to afford basic necessities, the last thing they need is to be yelled at or treated disrespectfully.

People who need food assistance deserve compassion, dignity, and respect. 😞

I unfortunately had a bad experience with this company/Nikki last week…

I have suspicions she did not come to walk my dog as planned. Unfortunately, my doorbell camera footage did not save at that time. She did not communicate with me following the “walk” (any walker I’ve ever had has given me atleast a photo and a check in regarding how it went (especially it being the first time) & if my dog peed/pooped).

I asked her how did the walk go & does she provide updates or photos to which she was very stand offish reporting “I don’t do updates. Unfortunately, when I was checking my cameras (living room) in real time during the day, I was able to see my dog had not moved off the couch (where he usually stays) all day. Additionally, it did not appear any of his things I prepared for the walk had been touched (for instance, his cooling vest which softens when wet- remained stone dry on my ottoman where I left it, leash & bowl untouched).

As a business owner who specializes in the care of animals and who reportedly has a dog of her own, I am shocked by how stand offish she was & unwilling to communicate or provide an update following the service.

For the next person who books with Nikki, I would request evidence she came for the scheduled walk & an update on how the walk went other than “it was fine.”

Despite this, I paid my bill but I will not book this person in the future.

First appointment, I was told my eye pressure was too high and it was suggested I get an SLT. I was not given an opportunity to ask questions and was rushed out of the room.

3 appointments were scheduled. I was told the first was for the SLT and the other two follow ups to measure eye pressure.

1 of 3 appointments, he took the tech putting in the drops I was nervous (because I got no explanation about the procedure). He offered a little reassurance. I had the procedure done. It was NOT pleasant at all. Felt like hot pokers being stuck in my eyes with the left one being worse. I immediately had the worst migraine I have had in my entire life which in the past I had ER visits for migraines. I was concerned I was going to vomit in the laser room. I was also very dizzy, disoriented, and unsteady on my feet. I was rushed out of the room. Prior to the laser, I was told by the admin that I had to stick around after the procedure to have my eye pressure rechecked and learned the Dr doesn’t bother to check for an eye pressure spike. Seems unethical and potentially dangerous.

Second visit today, I was expecting an eye pressure reading and learned I would have another SLT. I’m sure glad I didn’t drive there because there would have been no way for me to drive home. There seems to be serious lack of information occurring at this centre and you are NOT given an opportunity to ask questions. I raised my concerns to the tech that I was not informed that I would be receiving the laser again. Had I been informed, I would have taken migraine medication to prevent a debilitating migraine. He told me to raise my concerns with the Ophthalmologist. I raised the concern about not being informed as well as concerns with my last SLT (dizzy, disoriented, and unsteady on my feet) and that I was rush out of the room. The ophthalmologist told me he does 60 SLT a day and no one has ever had issues except for me. I was lied to because there was a patient in the waiting room that he lasered that had an increased spike in eye pressure post procedure. I was told he had never heard of anyone who had experienced what I had experienced (possibly because we are rushed out so he can bring in another person, zero opportunities for feedback). He gave me the option to reschedule but I was already there and that in the next week I would begin my post secondary practicum therefore it would not be ideal to reschedule. He did the procedure and it felt like hot pokers being inserted in my eyes. The left worst that the right. I felt like saying stop I’m done. I experienced an instant migraine, nausea, disorientation, and dizziness. I immediately told him what had occurred and he gaslit me telling me what I had experienced was stress related. I responded funny the migraine was not there prior to this procedure. He told me going forward the risks outweigh the benefits for this procedure and that it shouldn’t be done again. He said this because I called him out for gaslighting me. He rushed me out and told me to go sit outside the room to recover a little bit before leaving. Once again, I was at risk for a fall. I have two knee replacement and osteoporosis, a fall would be devastating. No eye pressure was taken post procedure. I guess it doesn’t matter if we patients have a spike in eye pressure and lose their eyesight.

I waited a little in the waiting room and then made my way to the admin where I informed her that I wanted to see another doctor for appointment number three. I informed her that I refuse to be gaslit by this doctor again. I was told she was not his admin and to call his admin on Monday.

I refuse to see this unethical, gaslighting, unprofessional doctor again. He will not put my health and safety at risk and gaslight me when I raise concerns.

Passing vulnerable, disabled individuals in crisis between firms using defective referrals, demanding upfront cash retainers without preliminary review, hanging up on callers, and fabricating follow-up documentation directly violates the Law Society of British Columbia Code of Professional Conduct regarding integrity, civility, quality of service, and candor. At 2:30pm a nurse pops up and declares that surgery can not be performed today due to Doc running into complications with previous surgery and “I “ will have to call her office to re book ( which means another 13 months of wait?). I was pissed at this moment. I asked her what was she waiting for till 2:30pm?
I booked time off work and I can not drive an hour back and forth for another 3 times. And moreover, will she compensate me for cancelling on me at the last moment? With IV inserted in my hand? Where is 48 hours cancellation policy now? It only applies to patients? Our time holds no value?
I am a healthcare professional myself and if I am running behind schedule …. I make sure I stay back to accommodate all the patients which were booked and definitely not cancel on them while they are sitting in the waiting area, and that is professionalism.
Definitely she doesn’t know what professionalism means.

I want to share my support for my wife and speak about the disappointment I have personally experienced throughout this difficult journey.

My wife had a high-risk pregnancy, and from the beginning we knew that our unborn daughter had a serious heart condition. We trusted the medical care we were receiving and hoped that, during such a frightening and emotional time, we would receive the attention, understanding, reassurance, and support that every family deserves.

Unfortunately, my wife did not feel that she received that level of care during the three appointments she had with Dr. Tuba Aksoy. As her husband and the father of our daughter, it was extremely difficult for me to watch her go through this experience while also dealing with the fear and uncertainty surrounding our baby’s condition.

After our daughter was born, she immediately required medical treatment because of her serious heart condition. Since then, she has undergone two heart surgeries, and she still has another surgery ahead of her.

No parent should have to watch their child go through something like this. As a father, seeing my daughter face major heart surgeries has been one of the most painful experiences of my life. During a time like this, families need compassion, understanding, communication, and genuine support from their healthcare providers.

I stand completely beside my wife and support her in sharing her personal experience. I understand her disappointment, and I share many of those concerns myself.

I am not sharing this simply out of anger. I am sharing it because I believe families deserve to feel heard, respected, and properly supported, especially when dealing with a high-risk pregnancy and a child facing a serious medical condition.

I sincerely hope that sharing our experience may help other parents feel empowered to ask questions, do thorough research, and seek a second or even third medical opinion when they feel it is necessary.

As a husband and father, I will always stand beside my wife and my daughter.

one_star_reviews.text: We had an extremely disappointing experience with Michelle Boehmer of Keller Williams Edge Realty. A 7 p.m. showing was booked at our home while my wife was 38 weeks pregnant and we had a toddler and two large dogs to manage, only for us to later learn that the people attending had already purchased a new-build home on our street and were simply looking at the finishes in our home for design ideas — not because they had any genuine interest in purchasing our property. Had we been told the true purpose of the visit, we never would have agreed to disrupt our family and leave our home for what was essentially a tour for design inspiration. In my opinion, using a scheduled real-estate showing in this manner was incredibly disingenuous and demonstrated a serious lack of professional judgment, respect and integrity. Sellers open their private homes with the reasonable expectation that the people coming through are legitimate prospective buyers, not individuals using an active listing as a showroom. I reached out directly to address what happened and, as of writing this review, I have received no meaningful response or acknowledgement of the concern and have seen no accountability. That lack of accountability has only reinforced my disappointment with how this was handled. Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend Michelle Boehmer or Keller Williams Edge Realty.

one_star_reviews.text:
STAY AWAY FROM PRIORITY PAY.

Our experience with this company felt like a complete scam and bait-and-switch.

They promised us one thing to get us signed up, and then charged us something completely different. We were told we would receive competitive rates, yet we ended up paying close to 5% in processing costs, far more than QuickBooks, Shopify, and other options.

And this was NOT just a verbal misunderstanding. We had revised rates and commitments IN WRITING, and they still did not honour them.

Charlie made the original promises. Once the billing problems started, dealing with David and Keyshawn became an absolute nightmare. Suddenly the fast communication we received when they wanted our business disappeared, and getting accountability or a proper resolution became almost impossible.

My advice to any business: DO NOT believe what Priority Pay offers you before you sign up. Even having it in writing did not protect us from this experience.

Check every single statement, fee and percentage because what you are actually charged may look nothing like what you were sold.

I would never use Priority Pay / Elavon again and would strongly warn other businesses to stay away.

An employee wearing a green hoodie with short hair immediately approached us and said, in a very abrupt and hostile manner, “No, no, no, no. You can’t be there.” I was caught off guard because I genuinely did not know I had entered a restricted area. I immediately stepped away and said, “ oh I’m sorry”

At that point, the situation should’ve ended. Instead, that employee continued to stare at me intensely and made comments about the register being right there and that there “should be a sign” indicating the area was restricted. I agreed with her and acknowledged that clearer signage would’ve prevented the misunderstanding. The store was completely unfamiliar to me and my friends and I was there to browse and look at merchandise NOT to find or access the register. Despite this, she continued standing staring at us while we were still simply looking at the bags since my friend wanted to purchase one similar to the one they had on the wall.

The issue was never that she corrected me. Staff ABSOLUTELY have the right to ask customers not to enter restricted areas. The issue was the UNECESSARILY hostile and INTIMIDATING manner in which she handled a simple misunderstanding. Once I stepped away and apologized, there was no reason for the interaction to continue in such a confrontational way. A simple, “Hi, this area is for staff only. Could you please step back?” would have resolved the situation immediately and respectfully. Instead, the employee’s tone, continued staring, and overall demeanor made my friends and I extremely uncomfortable. We ultimately decided to leave without purchasing anything. Mistakes and misunderstandings happen. What matters is how they are handled. This could have been handled with basic respect, dignity, clear communication, and de-escalation. I hope management takes this as an opportunity to remind staff that correcting a customer does not require making them feel intimidated or unwelcome. Clear signage and respectful communication would have prevented this entire situation. We came in excited to shop and support the store, but unfortunately left with a very negative impression because of how this interaction was handled.

Five of their children have now left home due to what they describe as unbearable conditions. There have also been reports of serious physical abuse, including injuries to the children. Very disappointing experience at the BC Liquor Store in Osoyoos, particularly because of the way the situation was handled by an employee named Agraz.

We made a purchase by credit card, and the customer-facing payment screen clearly showed that the transaction had been approved. Another employee also saw that the screen showed “approved,” and I showed them the transaction on my credit card account as well. As is normal with many credit-card purchases, the transaction was still listed as “pending,” since transactions can remain pending for a few days before being fully posted.

Despite this, Agraz handled the situation in an unnecessarily aggressive and confrontational manner. Her tone was extremely loud, instructive, and judgmental, to the point that it felt more like being spoken down to or bullied than being helped as a customer. There was very little effort to calmly explain what the issue was or acknowledge that, from our side, both the payment terminal and credit-card account indicated that the transaction had gone through.

I understand that payment-processing issues can happen and that employees need to follow store procedures. That is not my complaint. My complaint is entirely about how we were treated while the issue was being resolved. Customers should be spoken to respectfully, especially when they have paid in good faith and are cooperating to resolve a technical or payment-processing issue.

one_star_reviews.text:
After two years, my sidewalk is falling apart.

Two years after having my sidewalks installed, I have significant spalling where the aggregate under the top layer is exposed. Large areas are flaking off/chipping in multiple areas. I contacted the company to request a quote on repairs, and it took over a month to get them out to my place.

Their estimator showed up for the appointment almost an hour late (I had to contact him to see if he was still coming), and told me the issue was caused by standing water freezing (there would be no standing water had they poured a proper grade), then using "ice melt" on those areas, except I never use deicing salts because it burns my dogs' feet. I told him this. There are also hairline cracks I have repaired, and holes I have had to fill.

He told me he would call Lefarge and get back to me. He didn’t. It took two more months to get a response, after which point he said he didn’t know how to make me happy and offered to seal the sidewalk for for $2.75/sq.ft. effectively giving me the option to give them more money to do another job poorly.

This summer, I could audibly hear crackling when I stepped on my sidewalk. As you can see from the video, the surface comes off with no effort, using just my fingernail.

Spalling is defined as "surface flaking, chipping, or pitting, primarily caused by water entering porous concrete, freezing, and expanding, aggravated by deicing salts, poor initial installation, or improper curing". Since I don't use the deicing salts, that leaves the issues entirely to poor installation.

I’ve had a bad feeling about these guys since they completed the initial job. There are globs of cement firmly adhered to my siding, and the workers knocked parging off the back of my house.

Back then, the same estimator refused to pick up the final payment despite telling me he would, instead having me leave work to deliver a bank draft to a Tim Hortons.

A cement mix and installation should be able to withstand Alberta winters, and a company with any integrity should stand by its work. Neither of those things happened.
Price assessment
Overpriced
Services
Concrete sidewalk building

For reasons we still don’t understand, the doctor flat out refused to take my uncle’s blood pressure. We understand this particular doctor has since relocated to the Pitt Meadows Superstore location. Please, stay away from this clinic and from this doctor if you care about the health of your loved ones.

one_star_reviews.text:
Honestly, the only redeeming quality at Syl's Drive In anymore is the ice cream. It genuinely always hits the spot and is the one thing I can count on. Beyond that, the food is just not worth it. You pay a premium for what feel like the tiniest burgers and meals imaginable. The fries are consistently hard, overly crunchy, and completely devoid of flavor – they taste like cardboard. While the burger itself has a decent flavor, it's so small it's gone in literally two bites.

And don't even get me started on the poutine. While it might look like a decent size initially, as soon as you get past the top layer of fries, the rest of it is completely dry with zero gravy and zero cheese. That's not how a poutine should be! It used to be packed full of gravy and cheese all the way to the bottom, but nowadays you just get the most plain, bland poutine ever for a really high cost.

My partner had ordered a plain burger, emphasizing no toppings, and it arrived fully loaded. This isn't an isolated incident either; errors with getting burgers wrong, like ordering something plain or with specific omissions, and receiving it fully loaded, are a consistent and unresolved issue. It's incredibly frustrating when you have dietary restrictions or preferences and your order comes out the exact opposite of what you asked for. How can an order be messed up so badly, and so consistently? It makes you wonder if the person taking the order isn't listening, or if the grill staff aren't reading the screen. This kind of basic error is unacceptable, and it really feels like the staff need proper training. Because this is a constant issue that happens all the time with syls.

The patties are tiny, the fillets are small, and the serving sizes are a shadow of what they once were. I remember when the mushroom boxes were filled to the brim; now you get maybe 7-10 small mushrooms. Ever since the new owners took over, everything has gone downhill drastically. The quality, taste, and value are just not what they used to be. I'm genuinely super disappointed with how terrible this place has become.

one_star_reviews.text:
My son has an opioid addiction, we almost lost him last year. He was 11 months clean and relapsed in June. I was desperate as we are when our children relapse and was actively searching for a good quality treatment that had availability immediately. I talked to Into Action and they sounded like they had an OK program and have been around for a long time. I choose to go with hirer priced program they offered “Inspire” in White Rock because they had 3 one on one counselling sessions a week and offered a few other things that the lower priced programs did not,  I felt my son would do better with the extras. I also ASSUMED the rooms and food would be better, they were not. The food is being delivered every day, not cooked in house, which is a huge surprise for my son, not the quality we expected.

They picked him up and took him to the home. Once he arrived, they made him sign their contracts, he was so high he was not capable reading or signing anything. Their contract states they were supposed to search his items, which they did not and left stuff on him, also in the contract was that they took his phone away for 7 days (very important part) on day 5 he calls me BECAUSE THEY GAVE HIM HIS PHONE, and says he is leaving, they have basically left him in a room for days detoxing by himself. So, he leaves…… I called them for my refund of $20,500, they said that my son signed a contract stating that they hold my money for 365 days and I had to wait this waiting period, but he is welcome back anytime. How can they have an intoxicated addict sign a financial contract, he did not pay for the treatment. I scaped together all that money and now paying interest on it while they hold it and MAKE interest on it!! He refuses to go back because of his treatment there and I cannot afford to send him anywhere else. They are supposed to be helping these addicts, that is the opposite of what they are doing. They have lost sight of what they are supposed to be doing , all they care about is the money!!

one_star_reviews.text:
It is honestly an art form how these places manage to completely erase the flavor profile of a piece of meat. You are talking about brisket—a cut of beef that is supposed to be brined, spiced, smoked, and steamed to perfection. It is meant to be a flavor bomb.

Instead, they somehow manage to extract all the seasoning, neutralize the fat, and leave you with a pile of lukewarm, grey matter that has the texture of an old sponge. It takes a monumental amount of corporate effort to make beef taste like absolutely nothing.

And the financial math of it is what really twists the knife. You stand there at the cash register, watching the numbers climb on the pin pad, and your brain justifies it by thinking, "Alright, it's a bit pricey, but I'm about to get a heavy, satisfying deli lunch." Then you finish the last bite, stare down at the greasy wax paper, and realize you feel exactly the same as you did thirty minutes ago—just poorer and deeply disappointed. It’s culinary gaslighting. You literally have to check your bank account afterwards just to confirm that the transaction actually happened, because your tastebuds have absolutely zero memory of it.You didn't even get the satisfaction of a bad meal that you can laugh about; you just got a void where a lunch should have been.
Up to 10 min

All concerns below were mentioned to the admin team and escalated via email in the weeks since. No attempts have been made by Clever to rectify the safety issues. Ultimately the administrative staff have ghosted us.

1) Carelessness with a food allergy
We notified Clever about our baby's food allergy during registration and were reassured that staff are trained to handle allergies. When we arrived the first morning we reminded the caregivers what he is allergic to. Despite this there were two exposure risks that happened. On the first morning I was handed the wrong bottle of milk or formula by a caregiver that didn't look at the clearly labelled bottle from the fridge. On the second day, when I asked what was spread on the toast being offered to my child the caregivers said they didn't know. It was clearly a dairy product and thankfully I was there to stop him before he ate it. The people caring for your children should show more awareness of what's being fed to them. Many parents bring pumped breastmilk to daycare with their babies, which adds an additional biohazard safety risk if caregivers aren't checking labels before giving bottles to the babies.

2) Choking hazard at snack time
Babies from 12-18 months were fed apple wedges/chunks. This is a choking hazard unless sliced very thinly and the two caregivers seemed unaware of this, which brings up a concern of their training around food safety and preventing choking in babies & toddlers.

3) Harsh behaviour with babies
I observed one caregiver make a snappy comment and roughly snatch a toy back from one child to give it back to another. These two babies appeared to be only about 1 year old. The same person was speaking harshly to get another baby to open his mouth during feeding later that day.

4) Comforting distressed babies did not feel reliable
I watched a baby around a year old crying inconsolably for a good part of the morning and minimal efforts were made to console him. Most kids cry at daycare, especially during the early introduction days, but It didn't seem like the Clever staff were very intuitive or reassuring when kids were upset. Parents need to be able to trust that daycare staff can recognize distress and respond in a way that comforts and nurtures their child.

5) Naptime (FYI if your baby still naps twice a day)
I asked what they do for babies who aren't on 1 nap/day yet and still need more sleep. The caregivers said that they would put the baby in a crib in the same room if they needed to sleep but that they would also leave the lights on and continue to play music until 12:30 when they put all the babies down for a nap. There isn't a separate space for 2-nap babies. I can't imagine any baby napping well in that stimulating environment.

6) Extreme cancellation policy compared to other daycares
The center’s cancellation documentation requests 60 days notice for refunds, which is significantly longer than the other daycares I’ve spoken to since this experience. Deposits for daycare and meal plans totaled over $1,300 and was required upfront before the orientation week. This is a large sum to attempt to retrieve in the event that you visit the center with your child and observe the same concerns we did.

one_star_reviews.text: I do not enjoy writing negative reviews, but staying silent here would be a betrayal of the sangat. The management of this place behaves in a way that is completely incompatible with Sikh principles. Khalsa stands for human rights, justice, and defending the oppressed — yet this institution refuses to support even the peaceful Sikh struggle for self‑determination. This is not neutrality — it is indifference toward suffering that our faith commands us to confront. The sangat comes here to bow before Sri Guru Granth Sahib, not to endorse a management that has abandoned its moral responsibility. It is time for the community to demand answers. The sangat must ask the hard questions: What is this institution doing — if anything — to uphold Sikh values and advance the Sikh cause?

I had a very disappointing experience at this Gurudwara last Sunday.

When I asked for a couple of extra naan/rotis, instead of being treated with kindness and respect, I received dirty looks and was told, “This is a Gurudwara, not your home, so please eat accordingly.”

I understand that langar is meant to be served fairly and that food should not be wasted. However, there is a respectful way to communicate that message. A Gurudwara should be a place where people feel welcomed, respected, and cared for—not embarrassed or judged for asking for a little extra food.

I have also seen reports about a similar situation at a Northeast Calgary Gurudwara, where someone asking for extra rotis was reportedly questioned about taking them for work. If volunteers are going to manage langar, proper guidance should be given to everyone about how to speak respectfully to sangat.

Management should take this seriously and ensure that all volunteers treat people with dignity and respect, regardless of what they are wearing, where they work, or how much food they ask for.

Langar is about seva, equality, humility, and kindness. Nobody should leave feeling humiliated for simply asking for food.

I hope the management addresses this and provides better guidance to the volunteers. If these kinds of experiences continue, I will consider sharing my experience publicly on social media so that people are aware of what happened.

Our experience with Glacier Cabs was extremely disappointing, especially as visitors from out of town.

We booked a cab to take us approximately 15 minutes up the road to our friends’ hotel. We were staying just outside Nelson toward Balfour. When the driver picked us up, the meter was already showing $97.

When we booked the cab, nobody informed us that a roughly 15-minute trip would cost $97. The driver explained that he had started the meter when he left downtown Nelson and that this was the standard rate we were required to pay. At that point, we had no other option and had to pay the full amount.

What makes this even more frustrating is that our friends used the same company and paid approximately $30 for their trip into Nelson, so we are unsure whether this is the standard practice or whether it was specific to our driver.

As visitors, we felt completely taken advantage of and were shocked by the lack of transparency around the pricing. If there are additional charges for the driver travelling to pick someone up, customers should be clearly informed of this when booking.

I would not recommend Glacier Cabs based on this experience. If you have no other transportation option, I would strongly recommend asking exactly what the fare will be before getting into the cab, especially if you are outside downtown Nelson.

one_star_reviews.text: Exceptionally bad …. Absolutely no way of getting connected to anybody. A doctor’s office should not be that hard to reach. The wait time is really long and on top of that there is a paid parking for which I was fined as I was with the doctor when parking time needed to be renewed.

This was probably one of the most disappointing and upsetting experiences I have ever had with a doctor.

I went to see Dr. Adam Telner after dealing with symptoms for nearly two years that have had a significant impact on my daily life, particularly my reaction to eating carbohydrates. I came to the appointment genuinely hoping that a specialist would listen to what I had been experiencing, ask questions, and help me understand what might be happening.

Unfortunately, I left feeling completely dismissed.

What was most difficult was not simply that Dr. Telner didn't have an immediate answer. I understand that medicine is complicated and that not every condition has an easy diagnosis or solution. What upset me was how little curiosity or empathy I felt toward understanding what I was experiencing.

Rather than feeling that my symptoms were being investigated, I felt I was essentially being told that sometimes people develop problems and simply have to live with them. After struggling with something that has affected my quality of life for such a long time, hearing that from a specialist without feeling that there had been a meaningful attempt to understand the cause was incredibly discouraging.

I left the appointment feeling ignored, dismissed, and, more than anything, helpless. That is a terrible feeling to have after seeking medical help from someone you hoped might finally be able to provide some answers or direction.

I very rarely write negative reviews because I understand how difficult it is to work with the public, especially in healthcare. But this experience affected me enough that I felt I should share it. Patients who are already struggling with unexplained symptoms deserve to feel heard, even when a doctor does not immediately know the answer.

I sincerely hope Dr. Telner reads this and reflects on how his communication and approach can affect patients who may already be frightened, exhausted, and simply looking for help.

Unfortunately, based on my experience, I cannot recommend Dr. Telner.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience with CNIH’s Dental Hygiene admissions

I would strongly recommend that international dentists think carefully before applying to CNIH’s Dental Hygiene program.

I am an internationally trained dentist and applied to the Dental Hygiene program after specifically asking the admissions advisor about my eligibility and chances as an international dentist. I had also heard concerns from other international dentists about their experiences with the admission process, so I made sure to ask directly before spending money and time on the application.

I was advised to complete the entrance exam and the mature student test, which involved a $150 entrance exam fee. I completed both and scored 84% on the entrance exam and 22 points on the mature student test.

I was then told that I had done very well in my interview and that my chances of being selected were high. I was therefore quite surprised to receive an email approximately two weeks later informing me that I had not been selected.

What was especially frustrating was that I already had several years of dental assisting experience in Canada, which I clearly explained during my interview. When I asked what I could do to strengthen my application, I was advised to shadow or work with a dentist—something I was already doing.

My biggest concern is the lack of transparency in the admissions process. If certain applicant backgrounds or previous dental education are not being considered competitively, applicants should be told clearly before they spend money on entrance testing and invest significant time in the application process.

I understand that admission to a competitive program is never guaranteed, and I respect the college's right to select candidates. However, applicants deserve clear and honest information about how their background and experience are evaluated.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend CNIH to international dentists without first getting very clear, preferably written, information from the admissions department about how internationally trained dentists are evaluated. I wish this had been made clear to me before I invested my time, money, and effort in the application process.

There were 2 cars in the lot that look like they haven't moved in months. There was another car that I had the feeling did not belong to a hikers. It felt like a parking lot from any true crime story you have ever watched.
I started into the path with my bear spray and a noise maker. I got about 20 m into the trail and my gut pleaded with me to turn around, so I did. There are so many y better trails within a close distance. I'd pass on Dezadeash!
Difficulty
Easy
Route type
Out-and-Back
Parking space
Plenty of parking
Parking options
Free parking lot
The parking lot is muddy and rusted with potholes. There is also a grassy area. Its not a popular trail with a steady stream of people coming and going, and it is behind what looks like an abandoned building. I didnt feel my car would be safe while I hiked. This is the first place in the Yukon to give me this feeling.
Fees
Restrooms
None available
Dog-friendliness
Keep your dog on a leash, for bear safety.

one_star_reviews.text: I was intrigued after reviewing Spergel's Facebook marketing so I inquired. Almost immediately, I began being harassed by telephone. Someone named Matthew. (sp?) called me incessantly at all hours and leaving recorded messages. I spoke to him at one time and told him that I had some free time to speak to him to hear what he had to say at 1 o'clock the next day. I advised him by text message of this. 1 o'clock came and went, and he didn't phone, however, his calls kept coming into my inbox. I am very busy in my work and don't have time to take un scheduled calls, let alone from someone who is so persistent and annoying.  After informing the caller that I do not want to hear from him on a couple of occasions, he persisted. I eventually had to report Spergel to the CRTC which regulates spam and telemarketers like this. Spergel has lost all credibility in my eyes and the company should be ashamed for using such high-pressure sales tactics for people who are facing debt problems and may be vulnerable.

Guess they have too many customers… I didn’t see any so, I am not sure but it was an hour before closing!

They must of thought I was not a serious buyer!

Too bad and so sad for them…. Do NOT go there for your business! I know I won’t go back again!

Your understanding of customer service is truly lacking!
I ended up going to Costco and bought two pairs of glasses. Their customer service and delivery was fantastic!!
Having said all that, good luck!

Scam pricing and pathetic scam of language on their website to target and make people vulnerable as you cannot upload anything following biometrics so you’re forced to pay their pricing.

Highly unprofessional.

Further, I found so many spelling mistakes on their emails and website. It literally looks like a scam. Not to mention making it so challenging to contact them, get information, find their office — can’t help but feel like this company is highly unethical.

0 stars. Do better.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m honestly so disappointed with the recent changes to Plant Veda’s Mango Lassi.

I’ve been buying this product since it first came on the market, and it used to be one of my favourites. It was rich, thick, creamy, and had the texture and flavour of an actual lassi. Unfortunately, the most recent packages I’ve bought are completely different -
it’s now extremely watery and has lost the rich texture that made it so good in the first place.

What’s even more concerning is that a couple of weeks ago, I opened a package that was completely covered in mold. This is extremely disappointing and, frankly, concerning from a food-safety perspective.

I really hope Plant Veda takes this feedback seriously. I understand that products can change, but this feels like a significant decline in both quality and consistency. I’ve supported this product since its launch, and I would genuinely love to see the original quality brought back.
